role.altitude: The chemistry lecturer keeps discussing with colleagues, judging students for references, interpreting course results and deciding in committees; arranging meetings by mail, digging up grades for letters, compiling course figures and reading long documents in full shrink.
skills_to_grow: Editing drafted letters and reports into their own judgement
role.ambitious_version: A lecturer whose reports and references take an hour, not an evening.

tasks.short: Arrange meetings, collaborate with colleagues to address teaching and research issues, share documents and data, and follow up on agreed actions.

steps.what: Lecturer collaborates with colleagues to address teaching and research issues
Lecturer shares documents and data with colleagues
Lecturer follows up on agreed actions

tasks.design: A scheduling poll finds meeting times, and a shared workspace per topic holds documents, data and an action list with owners and dates, instead of mail threads with attachments. Discussing and agreeing stay with the colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings and material moved by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling polls and shared workspaces with action lists.
tasks.still_hard: Colleagues at other institutions on other systems.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a reluctant colleague to share instrument time.

reach.learn: Whether actions are completed more often.

evidence.claim: Scheduling polls and shared workspaces replace mail threads.

assumptions: Boundary: collaborating with colleagues; serving on committees (task 5883) is a sibling task.

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the shared action list current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few joint projects; high: many joint teaching and research issues.

tasks.short: Receive the student's request with CV and deadline, gather grades and work, judge what to say, write letters of recommendation for students, check and sign them, and submit them.

steps.what: Student submits the request form with CV, transcript, target and deadline
Lecturer gathers the student's grades, project work and own notes
Lecturer judges what to say about the student
Lecturer writes the letter of recommendation

loop.input: The lecturer's key points about the student and the student's CV and target programme.
loop.output: A draft letter in the lecturer's structure.
loop.check: Every claim about the student must come from the lecturer's key points or the records; the lecturer rewrites the judgement in their own words.
loop.stop: The lecturer keeps the letter, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each letter speaks to one student and one programme.

steps.what: Lecturer checks and signs the final letter
Lecturer submits the signed letter to the programme or employer

approvals.approved_version: The letter as signed by the lecturer in s5, addressed to the programme or employer named in the student's request; any edit needs a new signature before submitting.

tasks.design: Students request a letter through a form with their CV, transcript, target and deadline, and the lecturer sees the student's grades and project work in one view instead of searching mails and lists. Judging what to say stays with the lecturer. A drafting step turns the lecturer's key points into a letter, every claim traceable to those points or the records, and the lecturer rewrites the judgement in their own words. The lecturer signs and submits that version. No software rates the student.
tasks.previous_blocker: Information was scattered and each letter was written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Request forms and drafting from the lecturer's own points.
tasks.still_hard: Students the lecturer knows only from a large class.
tasks.human_edge: Saying something specific that makes a committee notice the student.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and typing; judgement stays.

reach.task: Apply for a programme or job

evidence.claim: Recommendation letters can be generated from templates and the teacher's input, with the teacher signing.
AI used for admission or evaluating learning is high-risk, so no model rates the student here.

assumptions: Boundary: writing recommendation letters; advising students on careers (task 5881) is a sibling task.
The student's form time is shown in s1 and is about what their request mail took.
Judging, signing and submitting keep their full time.
research_questions: Are letters submitted before deadlines more often?

incremental.description: Lecturer keeps the request form current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few letters for well-known students; high: many letters in application season.

tasks.short: Collect course figures, interpret results and decide improvements, write the report narrative, check the final report, and submit required reports related to instruction.

steps.what: Lecturer collects course figures: enrolment, pass rates, grade distribution and evaluation scores
Lecturer interprets the results and decides improvements
Lecturer writes the narrative of the course report

loop.input: The course figures from the dashboard and the lecturer's conclusions.
loop.output: A draft narrative in the report template.
loop.check: Every number in the text must match the dashboard; the lecturer rewrites the conclusions in their own words.
loop.stop: The lecturer keeps the narrative, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each course run has its own story behind the figures.

steps.what: Lecturer submits required reports related to instruction to the quality office

approvals.approved_version: The report text and figures as checked by the lecturer in s4; any edit needs a new check before submitting.

tasks.design: A course dashboard combines enrolment, pass rates, grade distribution and evaluation scores from the learning platform and student system, instead of the lecturer compiling them in a spreadsheet. Interpreting results and deciding improvements stay with the lecturer. A drafting step writes the narrative in the report template from the dashboard figures and the lecturer's conclusions, with every number matching the dashboard. The lecturer checks the report and submits that version through the quality office's upload page.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were compiled by hand and narratives written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Course dashboards and drafting checked against the figures.
tasks.still_hard: Courses with small numbers where figures mislead.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a pass rate dropped in a way the committee accepts.
tasks.altitude: Less compiling and typing; interpretation stays.

reach.learn: Whether reports arrive complete and comparable.

evidence.claim: An assessment platform provides item statistics per question.
A dashboard plus a bounded model drafting narrative with every number checked works for reports.

assumptions: Boundary: instruction reports; revising curricula (task 5875) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: grades and evaluations held in the learning platform and student system.
Interpreting, checking and submitting keep most of their time.
research_questions: Are reports submitted on time more often?

incremental.description: Lecturer checks dashboard figures against the source before use.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: data spread over systems; high: all figures in one dashboard.

tasks.short: Read meeting documents, serve on academic or administrative committees that deal with institutional policies and academic issues, and prepare written comments on proposals.

steps.what: Lecturer reads committee documents and proposals

loop.input: Long policy documents and proposals for the meeting.
loop.output: A short summary per document with the decisions asked and page references.
loop.check: Each summary point must cite a page; the lecturer reads the pages behind every decision asked.
loop.stop: Documents the summary cannot handle are read in full.
loop.why_not_simpler: Proposals vary in length and structure.

steps.what: Lecturer serves on the committee: discusses and decides on institutional policies and academic issues
Lecturer prepares written comments on proposals

tasks.design: A summary step gives a short overview per committee document with the decisions asked and page references, and the lecturer reads the pages behind each decision rather than every page. Comments are made in the shared document instead of separate mails. Discussing and deciding stay fully with the committee.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every document was read in full.
tasks.enabler_now: Summaries with page references and shared documents.
tasks.still_hard: Proposals where the detail is the point.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what a policy will do to students in practice.

evidence.claim: A university chat platform is available to staff in a pilot.

assumptions: Boundary: committee work; administrative duties as department head (task 5887) is a sibling task.
Discussing and deciding keep their full time.
research_questions: Does reading time fall without missed issues?

incremental.description: Lecturer checks summaries against key pages.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short documents; high: long policy packs.
